body:
We make Kiron, so weigh this accordingly. Everything here about StrongLifts comes from its App Store listing, its website and support pages, and recent App Store reviews, checked November 15, 2026. Everything about Kiron describes version 1.2.

StrongLifts' 5×5 hasn't changed. The price of entry has: the free tier ended in 2025, and the Power Pack many long-time lifters bought no longer covers the app. If you're deciding whether to pay up or move on, here's how Kiron (that's us) compares, and when staying is the right call.

StrongLifts or Kiron? The short version

  • Choose Kiron if you want a 5×5 that still works out every weight for you, for less: {{kiron:price-annual}}, against StrongLifts' $59.99. When 5×5 stops working, {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs are waiting.
  • Stay with StrongLifts if you want the app to lower the weight when you stall, very small weight jumps or an Apple Watch app, or you own Power Pack and can get half off your first year.
  • Export your StrongLifts history first, whichever you pick. Kiron can't import it, but you can type your working weights into your first workout.

Bottom line: both apps run the same simple 5×5 and do the math for you. StrongLifts is built around that one program. Kiron runs it for less, starts new lifters light on purpose, and has somewhere to go when it stalls. For most lifters, we think that's the better deal.

What Kiron is

Kiron is a workout app for {{kiron:cell-platforms}} that runs a training program for you. Start in one of three ways:

  • Pick one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs by goal, from Beginner 5×5 to muscle-building and running plans.
  • Answer a few questions and Kiron builds one.
  • Bring your own plan. Paste it from ChatGPT, a coach or a website, or snap a photo, and Kiron turns it into a program on your calendar.

Then there's little to think about:

  • Your next workout is ready when you open the app, whether you train on set days or whenever you make it to the gym.
  • Every weighted lift starts with a weight, and a new one comes with a short note saying why. After a set, Kiron asks how it felt and adjusts the rest.
  • Your weights go up as you get stronger, and Kiron tells you why: "You hit every set, so we added 5 lb."
  • Variety that keeps your main lifts, plus saved gyms for travel: switch to a hotel gym and Kiron swaps in exercises that fit.
  • Runs and races on the same calendar as your lifting, from a first 5K to a marathon.
  • Recovery that counts your other workouts, like runs saved to Apple Health or Health Connect.
  • {{kiron:progress-lead}} {{kiron:progress-detail}} {{kiron:progress-import}}
  • {{kiron:offline-lead}} {{kiron:offline-detail}}
  • Less than StrongLifts' yearly plan: {{kiron:price-annual}}, against $59.99.

The same 5×5, with every weight still worked out

StrongLifts' pitch is simplicity: one proven program, every weight worked out, so you just show up and lift. Kiron's Beginner 5×5, its own program built on the same classic structure, keeps that promise:

  • Two workouts, taking turns. Workout A is squat, bench press and barbell row, five sets of five; Workout B is squat, overhead press and one set of five deadlifts. Three a week, about 45 minutes each, with a barbell and a rack.
  • Train whenever you get there. Beginner 5×5 starts in Whenever I train mode: the next workout waits as "Up next", and nothing is ever marked missed. Prefer Monday, Wednesday and Friday? Switch to Fixed days, and Kiron can move missed ones forward.
  • A light first day. With no history in Kiron, you start the squat, bench press and overhead press on the empty bar, and the row and deadlift light. A short note explains why and adds: "Lifted before? Tell us after your first set and we'll move the rest up."
  • A quick climb if you're not new. After each set, Kiron asks how the weight felt. Tap "Too easy" and the rest of today's sets go up straight away: on a squat, 45 lb, then 55, 70, 85 and 105 lb if you keep saying so. Your next workout picks up where you finished.
  • Then weight goes on every workout. Get all your reps and next time is 5 lb (2.5 kg) heavier, or a bigger step if you had reps to spare. Miss a rep and the weight stays the same. The squat is in both workouts, so it climbs every session.

Both apps keep the weight the same after a miss, ease you back in after a long break, and list your warm-up sets and the plates for each side of the bar.

When 5×5 stalls, you don't need another app: Novice Linear Progression drops to three sets of five, Wave Loading Strength gets heavier in three-week waves, and Upper / Lower Strength spreads heavy lifting over four days. Your lift history comes along. For plans that run in blocks, see our guide to following a multi-phase plan without a coach.

How StrongLifts went subscription-only

StrongLifts' own support article on Power Pack, updated October 7, 2026, tells the story:

  • 2010 to 2014: the app is free. In 2014 comes Power Pack, a one-time $9.99 add-on for warm-ups, the plate calculator and extra exercises. Logging stays free.
  • May 2018: Power Pack sales stop and a Pro subscription begins.
  • June 2020: a Pro Lifetime plan is added.
  • 2023: the app starts calling Power Pack "lifetime," wording the article now calls a mistake.
  • 2025: Power Pack is retired and the free tier ends. Power Pack owners get 50% off their first year.

StrongLifts says hosting, development and support are ongoing costs that a one-time purchase doesn't cover. Reviewers noticed: of 317 App Store reviews at one to three stars from August 2025 to November 2026, 259 mention price or the subscription, and 101 mention lifetime or Power Pack. Several say they hit the paywall only after a recent update.

Prices vary by country and offer. To pay monthly, StrongLifts' help article suggests starting the yearly trial, cancelling before day 7, then switching to monthly in Settings.

Kiron costs less on both plans: {{kiron:price-annual}} against $59.99, and {{kiron:price-monthly}} against $11.99. Its 7-day free trial covers either plan; StrongLifts' covers only the yearly one.

Moving your 5×5 to Kiron

  1. Save your StrongLifts history. In Settings, tap Export Data, then Share, to email yourself a spreadsheet file (CSV). Stuck on the paywall? Tap the menu icon at the top right, then Contact Support, and send the pre-filled email to yourself; the file comes with it.
  2. Start Beginner 5×5. Pick it from Kiron's ready-made programs, choose Whenever I train or Fixed days, and tap Start this program.
  3. Set your weights on day one. Kiron can't read StrongLifts' file, so it starts you light. Type in the weights you were lifting, a little lighter after time off, or tap "Too easy" after each set and let the rest climb.
  4. Cancel StrongLifts where you subscribed, before it renews.

Kiron has no export of its own, so keep that file. Our guide to exporting your workout history covers other apps too.

Who should stay with StrongLifts

  • You want stalls handled for you. After repeated misses, StrongLifts lowers the weight by an amount you set, say 15% after two failed attempts. In Kiron, lowering it is up to you.
  • You want very small jumps. StrongLifts can add as little as 1 lb every three workouts, using fractional plates. Kiron adds 5 lb (2.5 kg) at a time.
  • You log from your wrist. StrongLifts' Apple Watch app, rebuilt in October 2026, can run a whole workout without your iPhone nearby. Kiron has no Watch app, and reads heart rate from Apple Health or Health Connect afterwards.
  • You own Power Pack. Send StrongLifts your old invoice for 50% off your first year, and your history comes back when the subscription starts.
  • You value a long track record. StrongLifts' app has been around since 2010 and has about 77,000 ratings on the US App Store, averaging 4.9. Kiron is new and still small.

StrongLifts questions, answered

Is StrongLifts still free?

No. Its support article says the app has been Pro only since 2025, and its App Store listing says it's "free to download, but requires a subscription to use." New users get a 7-day trial on the yearly plan.

What happened to Power Pack, and is there a lifetime plan?

Power Pack was retired in 2025, and its owners get 50% off their first year of Pro. The support article says the 2020 Pro Lifetime plan is still offered, but on November 15, 2026 the US App Store listed five-year plans at $199.99 and $239.99, and nothing named lifetime. Ask StrongLifts which one you're buying.

Is there a free 5×5 app?

Boostcamp's free tier has no time limit and lists free 5×5 programs from its community, but the feature that adds weight for you is part of Pro ($59.99 a year). A notebook or spreadsheet works too; our comparison of spreadsheets and workout apps covers the trade-off. {{kiron:free-tier-sentence}}

Can I take my StrongLifts history with me?

Yes, as a spreadsheet file, even from behind the paywall; the steps are above. Kiron can't import it, so type your current weights into your first Kiron workout.

Is StrongLifts good for beginners?

It's built for them: its App Store listing says it's made for lifters starting or returning to barbell training, and it works out every weight. The open question is the price, not the program.

If StrongLifts' price is why you're here, try Kiron's Beginner 5×5: type in your current weights or start light, and Kiron adds weight from there. {{kiron:cta-sentence}} Get Kiron.

If StrongLifts' stall handling and Watch app are what you'd miss, paying for it is a fair call.
